payload.title: [calls-correctness-1] Call creator can never join their own call (excluded from invitees, join requires an invite)
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING calls-correctness-1 (medium/correctness, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/calls/call-control-plane.ts
LINES: 244-250, 313-345, 636-649

WHAT: createCall strips the creator from invitees (`.filter((u) => u !== actor.userId)`, line 244) and writes invites only for invitees. joinCall and acceptInvite both call #requireInvitee(actor.userId) (lines 315, 345), which throws CallAuthzError('notInvitee') when no CallInvite row exists for the actor (lines 636-648). Since the creator has no invite row, the creator cannot acceptInvite or joinCall their own call. There is no creator special-case anywhere except endCall. The room only transitions ringing→active on the first invitee join, so the creator can never become a CallParticipant nor get a media join grant.

IMPACT: Core call flow is broken: the user who starts a call cannot participate in it (no participant record, no media grant). The call can only ever contain invitees, and a 1:1 call the creator started is unusable by the creator. Functional defect on the primary use case.

SUGGESTED FIX: Treat the creator as an implicit participant: either auto-create a self-invite/participant for the creator at createCall time, or special-case #requireInvitee to allow room.createdBy. Then joinCall must issue the creator a media grant like any other participant.
